subject.title: fix: stop doctor misreporting trusted-proxy gateways as unauthenticated

question: Should `openclaw doctor` classify a complete, runtime-usable trusted-proxy configuration on an exposed Gateway as authenticated-with-warning instead of unauthenticated-and-critical?
rationale: The patch's technical safety is anchored to existing runtime validation, but the severity downgrade is a user-facing security-diagnostic policy choice that code review cannot make unilaterally.

options.title: Accept the guarded warning path
options.body: Merge the runtime-aligned doctor classification so complete trusted-proxy deployments retain exposure guidance without token-repair advice.

options.title: Keep the critical diagnostic
options.body: Retain the current CRITICAL classification if maintainers want all non-loopback trusted-proxy deployments to require explicit manual security review regardless of runtime validity.

recommendation.title: Accept the guarded warning path
recommendation.body: Merge the runtime-aligned doctor classification so complete trusted-proxy deployments retain exposure guidance without token-repair advice.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged trusted-proxy hardening work defines the fail-closed source-validation invariant that this diagnostic now relies on.
